title: ESA BIC Andalucia — space startup incubation, autumn 2026 application round
funder: ESA BIC Andalucia / local programme operator
description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-09-28T14:53:44+02:00 The Open Call for Proposals is now OPENNext cut-off date: 30 October 2026 at 12:00 CET. Download the Application Package below to apply to ESA BIC Andalusia Download the Application Package (.zip)Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsThe Open Call for Proposals is OPEN. All application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. Download the Application Package (.zip)Prepare Your ApplicationBefore you begin filling out any forms, it is strongly recommended that you carefully read all the provided documents. Application Templates The Application Package contains the following documents: ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call (call conditions and process) ESA BIC Application Form (the document to complete and submit, including its annexes) Draft Incubation Contract Space Connection Assessment Supporting Documents Make sure to thoroughly review all supporting documents, particularly the Draft Incubation Contract. This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. Once everything is in order, submit the completed Application Form as a single PDF file to opencall-esabic-andalusia@catec.aero, with the subject ‘ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call’. Important: Ensure your submission is completed before the announced cut-off date. Submissions received after the cut-off deadline will not be considered for that particular round. Evaluation ProcessAfter submitting your application to ESA BIC Andalusia, the post-submission process is as follows: TOB Review: Your application first undergoes an initial screening by the Tender Opening Board (TOB). The TOB checks the completeness of your application and whether it meets the formal requirements. TEB Evaluation: If the TOB process is successful, your application is then forwarded to the Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). The TEB is composed of representatives from the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), ESA BIC Andalusia, the Junta de Andalucía as regional co-funder, and external experts. This board will conduct a detailed evaluation of your proposal, focusing on technical feasibility, business potential, and alignment with the goals of the ESA BIC programme. Interview with TEB: As part of the TEB evaluation, you will be invited to present your business idea. This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. TEB Decision & Certificate: Once the TEB has completed its evaluation and your interview, you will be formally notified of the outcome. If approved, ESA will issue your official TEB Selection Certificate, confirming your eligibility to secure the Junta de Andalucía’s co-financing approval prior to final contract signature. Detailed instructions for the co-financing application process follow. Contract Signing: Once the contract is signed, your startup officially begins its incubation period with ESA BIC Andalusia. Regional Co-Funding ApplicationAfter receiving your TEB Selection Certificate, you must submit your regional co-funding application via the Junta de Andalucía’s e-Office portal before the deadline indicated in the Call to secure co-funding from the regional authority. Complete the non-competitive grant form as established in the Open Call documentation and the referenced Regulatory Bases, attach your TEB Selection Certificate and all required administrative documents, and submit through the official channel. Regional co-funding is awarded to projects that have passed the TEB evaluation and meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in the Open Call and Regulatory Bases. Applications are processed in order of validation and subject to budget availability. You will then be notified of the award decision. Sign Contract & Start IncubationUpon confirmation of your regional co-funding, you will sign the Incubation Contract. With your signature in place, your incubation officially begins, granting you access to a comprehensive suite of programme services—high-level mentoring, state-of-the-art technical facilities, expert business coaching, dedicated legal & IPR support, the 60K € financing package, dynamic networking events, and community collaboration opportunities. Welcome aboard: incubation officially starts! Open Call for ProposalsESA BIC Andalusia operates under a continuous Open Call system, meaning that applications are accepted year-round. Proposals are evaluated at specific cut-off dates. The Open Call is now OPEN. Next cut-off date: 30 October 2026 at 12:00 CET. Download the Application Package above and submit your proposal to participate in the next evaluation round. Need Assistance?If you have any questions or require further clarification, please contact the ESA BIC Andalusia team directly. You are also encouraged to consult the FAQ for additional guidance and information. Contact the ESA BIC Andalusia teamConsult the Frequently Asked Questions

description: Apply - Aeropuerto ESA-BIC <iframe src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/ns.html?id=GTM-WX62QL34" height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe> Application process ESA BIC Valencia Region has a Permanent Open Call, for space related start-ups to apply. be part of the future Who can apply Spanish registered companies, located in the Valencia regions of Castellón, Alicante or Valencia. New or existing companies less than 5 years old Demonstrable space connection Viable Business Plan APPLICATION FIELDS Does your business have a space connection? We’re looking for teams, or start ups up to 5 years old, to use space technologies on non-space innovative solutions, or exploit non-space technology in the space market. Our incubated start ups will have wide access to an extensive innovation ecosystem thanks to the support of the Spanish Space Agency, the European Space Agency and all the ESA BIC Valencia Region partners Read the ESABIC Valencia Region Space Connection Assessment (download) The projects may target either upstream or downstream application fields. See some examples here: Downstream application fields Earth observation Satellite communication Mobility Agriculture Energy Robotics/Mechatronics or Materials Environmental monitoring Satellite navigation (road, sea, air) or Mobile services Upstream application fields Launchers Satellites Ground systems Human spaceflight Reply APPLICATION GUIDE How to apply The call for applications is open on an ongoing basis. Selection and evaluation of applications are scheduled periodically with deadlines posted on this website (typically three cut-offs are made per year). 01 Before applying, please contact us for introducing your project and receiving all information about the program. 02 Download and read the Open Call Documents. 03 Submit your project within the deadline using the following link Electronic Office AEROCAS attaching the following documents: Application Form Space Connection Assessment Open Call Template 04 If necessary, you will be asked to submit additional details/clarifications before admission to the Selection Board. 05 If accepted, you will be able to pitch your project and present your company to the Tender Evaluation Board. 06 In case of approval, sign the incubation contract and get ready to work with us! Application deadline Don’t miss our next application deadline 18th December 2026 12:00 midday DAYS : HOURS : MINUTES : SECONDS
